title: Clark Middle School celebrates first Hispanic Art Festival
excerpt: Clark Middle School held its first Hispanic Art Festival this week, with about 80 students across six art classes showcasing handmade piñatas, jarrones and a Día de los Muertos altar.
content:
Clark Middle School celebrated student creativity and border culture this week during its first Hispanic Art Festival, according to United Independent School District.

Organized by art teacher Miriam Gonzalez, the event showcased handmade piñatas, jarrones and a Día de los Muertos altar created by students.

Approximately 80 students across six art classes, mostly eighth graders and one sixth-grade class, worked on the projects. Using recycled materials already available on campus, students crafted and painted the pieces by hand, with some staying after school to finish decorations and paintings.

Gonzalez said the goal was to celebrate the community, the students and the culture of the border, and that it is important for students to learn to respect and appreciate art and help each other out, even when people do not always agree.

Gonzalez thanked the campus team, parents, bands, dancers and students who made the festival possible. Their contributions included preparing food, setting up displays and cutting and sanding wood for the altars.

Source: United Independent School District, November 5, 2026.
